subject: Urgent: LedgerCore production throttle & error spike — coordination
messages:
From: Anika Shah <anika@ledgercore.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: payments+ops@ledgercore.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error-rate / latency spike on reserved pool — production impacting

Diego,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and tail latency on our reserved capacity at ~08:45 PT. This is affecting authorization flows for a subset of high-volume merchants (approx 6% of traffic) — customers are reporting timeouts and failed captures.

Quick details:
- Error rate: from ~0.2% to 6.1% over 10 minutes
- p95 latency: jumped from 130ms to ~1.1s
- Traffic: short burst to ~2.8x usual QPS for our reserved routes

We flagged this in our ops channel and also opened a support ticket but wanted to loop you directly given the potential business impact (reconciliation windows shortly). Can Redwood confirm whether the dedicated GPU pool serving our reservation is saturated or if there was any auto-fallback activity?

Logs attached (small snippet). Please advise immediate mitigation steps — we can divert some traffic to hosted routes if you recommend.

Thanks,
Anika Shah
Head of Payments Operations
LedgerCore

Attachments: log_snippet.txt
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika@ledgercore.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error-rate / latency spike on reserved pool — production impacting

Anika —

Thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I’ve looped in Monica from Customer Success and Priyom from our runtime team so we can triage immediately. First priority: stabilize traffic and stop merchant-facing failures.

Planned immediate actions (doing now):
- Monica: run session-level routing to divert a controlled 20% of your low-risk traffic to hosted API while we triage reserved pool behavior
- Priyom: confirm pool utilization metrics and whether any allocation/eviction events occurred at 08:40–09:00 PT
- I’ll coordinate progress updates and keep your ops channel informed

Please ping me if you see new errors; we’ll share a short status update within 20 minutes.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Anika Shah <anika@ledgercore.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error-rate / latency spike on reserved pool — production impacting

Anika, Diego —

Quick update from CS side. I’ve kicked a routing rule to shift ~20% of non-auth-critical traffic to our hosted endpoints (we’ll only move requests that match your low-risk merchant list). This should reduce pressure on the reserved pool within 2–3 minutes. I’ve also temporarily bumped the retry window and disabled aggressive batching for the diverted traffic to keep latency predictable.

I attached a chart from your traffic dashboard showing the burst (traffic_chart.png). Priyom — any signal on the GPU-side?

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: traffic_chart.png
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Anika Shah <anika@ledgercore.com>
Cc:
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error-rate / latency spike on reserved pool — production impacting

Diego / Monica / Anika —

Preliminary runtime analysis:
- Observed sustained GPU utilization spike on LedgerCore’s reserved pool starting 08:42 PT concurrent with the QPS burst. Utilization peaked at ~98% for a 3-node shard set.
- Several inference worker processes hit OOM and were restarted; kernel-level evictions occurred which increased latency while KV caches warmed back up.
- No config changes detected in your reservation; autoscaler did not trigger new capacity because the pool was pinned and reserve headroom was low.

Immediate mitigations we’re enacting now:
1) Expand your reserved pool by adding 1 temporary burst node (warmup in progress) — ETA ~7 minutes to be fully available
2) Enable priority routing: critical merchant traffic stays on reserved nodes; lower-risk routes will continue to divert to hosted
3) Apply a conservative quantization profile for shortest-path models used by your auth flows (drop quality slightly to reduce memory footprint)

We’ll keep monitoring for further OOMs. I’m collecting the worker logs and included a short snippet in the ticket (SERV-879).

Priyom Das
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Attachment: log_snippet.txt
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Anika Shah <anika@ledgercore.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: High error-rate / latency spike on reserved pool — production impacting

Marissa —

Forwarding a live customer incident with LedgerCore (enterprise, high-velocity payments). Summary: reserved pool saturated by a short traffic burst, several inference workers OOMed and restarted, causing elevated 5xx and tail latency. We’ve applied immediate mitigations (20% routing diversion to hosted, temporary burst node, low-cost quantization).

Why I’m escalating to you: LedgerCore is sensitive to failed authorizations during peak windows. They’re asking for a short-term SLA adjustment and a mitigation credit if we don’t meet reconciliation SLAs for the period. They’re also asking for confirmation of a post-mortem and a commitment that reserved pools will not be oversubscribed in future.

Attached: mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf (MAV with remediation steps and timeline).

Request: Can we get exec-level approval to:
- Approve one-off credit (up to 5% of the monthly committed spend) conditionally if reconciliation is impacted
- Fast-track a reserved-capacity headroom policy change to guarantee an extra 10% buffer for LedgerCore while we complete a longer-term autoscaling improvement

I’ll join the after-action call with the LedgerCore ops team at 13:00 PT.

—Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Anika Shah <anika@ledgercore.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 16:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: High error-rate / latency spike on reserved pool — production impacting

Diego / team / Anika —

Thank you for the quick containment and clear remediation steps. Top-level guidance:
- Approve the one-off credit up to 5% of monthly committed spend if LedgerCore’s reconciliation window shows measurable impact. Finance will retroactively sign off; Diego, coordinate required approval paperwork with Legal & Finance (loop me if timeline slips).
- Immediate change: grant LedgerCore a temporary headroom of +10% on their reserved allocation for the next 72 hours (Ops, please confirm capacity is available). Priyom — prioritize the warm node assignment and keep me posted on OOM risk.
- Post-incident: we’ll schedule a formal post-mortem with LedgerCore next week and deliver a timeline for autoscaler improvements and stronger reserved headroom policies.

Anika — we want to restore confidence quickly. Monica, please provide LedgerCore with a short customer-facing summary and an estimated time to full recovery. Diego, I’ll join the follow-up call if helpful.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success Operations (interim)
Redwood Inference
